name: Claude Code
summary: Knows when a Claude Code session is blocked on you, finishes, or picks up again.
description: A Claude Code hook that turns three moments into metadata events: a session needs your answer (a permission prompt or a question), a session finishes its turn, and you reply. Replying closes that session's open loop on its own. Each session is identified by a 16-character hash; nothing you or Claude wrote leaves the hook, and it never blocks Claude Code: it runs asynchronously, times out after 1.5 s and always exits cleanly.

emits.when: A session is waiting on a permission prompt or a question for you
You send that session a prompt, which closes its open loop

neverSends: Claude's replies, or the text of any notification
Tool inputs, commands or their output
File paths, the working directory or the transcript path
Session titles or raw session ids (only a 16-character hash)

setup.title: Add the hook to your Claude Code settings
setup.body: Merge this into ~/.claude/settings.json to cover every project, or into .claude/settings.json in one project. The path and URL are already filled in for this machine. If you set FOCUSDECK_SENSOR_TOKEN on the server, add it under "env" as well.

setup.title: Start a new Claude Code session
setup.body: Hooks load when a session starts. Inside Claude Code, /hooks lists what's registered.

test.expect: "focusdeck-hook: sent … -> 200" on stderr, this connector turns live here, and "Claude Code · session … finished" appears in Today's log.
